title: Researchers Cut Quantum Circuit Complexity By 26x For Molecules
key_facts: Paper 'Hardware-Efficient Ground-State Preparation using Variational Imaginary-Time Majorana Evolution' (arXiv 2610.01954) by researchers at IQM Quantum Computers (Santona, Algaba, Anuar, Wernbacher, Sharma) and Fedor Simkovic.
The method, VIME, pre-trains a quantum circuit with a classical computer method (Majorana Propagation) and pairs it with a compressed 'tiled Unitary Product State' circuit design.
On the ruthenium complex TLD-1411, using up to 52 qubits, it reached chemical precision, with energy errors about 400 times smaller than earlier ADAPT-VQE-based methods.
Results matched highly accurate DMRG reference energies for that molecule.
On acene molecules needing up to 60 qubits, accuracy was comparable while using up to 26 times fewer CNOT gates and a 167-fold reduction in two-qubit gate depth.
The authors say it has so far been compared mainly with earlier ADAPT-VQE-type methods and needs further validation against other leading approaches and more kinds of molecules.
The article does not say whether the calculations ran on quantum hardware or on simulators.
quote_evidence: Energy errors in calculations on a ruthenium complex have been reduced approximately 400 times utilising a new method compared to earlier ADAPT-VQE based techniques; this level of precision was previously unattainable with existing quantum computational approaches requiring similar qubit numbers.
The authors note further validation against other state-of-the-art approaches is needed to fully establish its performance across diverse systems.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheaper circuits for molecule simulation could bring useful quantum chemistry closer, but the gains are measured against one earlier method.
event_date: arXiv paper 2610.01954 (October 2026); exact posting date not stated.
notes: Preprint, company research (IQM). Article is repetitive and inconsistent about the earlier method's name (ADAPT-VQE vs 'ADAPT-VMPE', likely a typo) and about '26 times' ('up to' vs 'as few as'); the 'up to' reading and ADAPT-VQE are used. Not stated whether run on real hardware.
